budget_feasibility.reasoning: Without verified data, estimating conservatively: 2 nights lodging in Lisbon (even bare-minimum hostels are realistically €40-60/night unverified, so ~€100-120 minimum); daily food for solo traveler doing 'local food' interest (€30-40/day conservatively, so ~€90 for 3 days); museum entries typically €8-15 each (estimate €30 for 2-3 visits); local transport passes/tickets (~€20-30); nightlife/drinks (~€30-40); coastal excursions or hiking transport (~€20-30). This totals roughly €600 minimum. The €500 budget is tight and would require hostels, self-catering some meals, and limiting paid activities — feasible only with significant compromises, not comfortably.

trip_summary: A 3-day Lisbon solo trip balancing coastal exploration, food culture, and nightlife under tight budget constraints (~€100 short of realistic minimum), working around the conflicting requirements of a 'packed pace' with mandatory late starts (no activities before 11am) and 3-hour afternoon rest blocks that together eliminate roughly half of each day — all pricing and logistics are unverified estimates, not confirmed facts.

key_decisions.decision: Flag the fundamental constraint conflict upfront rather than pretend it doesn't exist
key_decisions.reasoning: A 'packed pace' is incompatible with starting at 11am and losing 3 hours mid-day to rest (effectively 11am-2pm, rest 2pm-5pm, resume 5pm onward gives only ~4-5 usable hours daily). A truly packed itinerary requires either earlier starts or no mandatory rest blocks. I'll plan to the literal constraints but this will feel sparse, not packed.
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Silently ignoring the rest requirement to create a 'packed' feel — rejected because hard constraints must be respected exactly.

key_decisions.decision: Prioritize coastal Belém district and Alfama historic quarter as the two focal areas, skipping inland Sintra day-trip
key_decisions.reasoning: Unverified assumption: Belém offers coastline + history + museums (likely Jerónimos Monastery, Tower of Belém, Maritime Museum); Alfama gives history + nightlife + local food (Fado houses, tascas). Sintra is stunning but a full-day commitment (unverified: ~40min each way by train, €5-10 return, sites €8-15 each) — impossible to fit meaningfully with 11am starts and 3-hour rest blocks, and would blow the tight budget.
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Doing Sintra on Day 2 — rejected because it requires early start to be worthwhile, conflicts with hard constraint, and adds €40-60 in costs.

key_decisions.decision: Allocate Day 1 to Belém (coastal focus), Day 2 to Alfama/downtown (history/food/nightlife), Day 3 morning departure buffer only
key_decisions.reasoning: With a 11am start and 3-hour rest block, each day yields ~5-6 usable hours. Belém is compact enough to cover in one afternoon/evening (unverified: tram 15E takes ~30min from downtown, museums close around 6pm typically). Alfama's steep streets suit evening wandering (Fado starts ~8-9pm unverified). Day 3 is a departure day with no time for activities (check-out, travel to airport).
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Trying to fit a coastal hike (e.g. Cascais coastal walk) — rejected because it requires a morning start and full day, both impossible here.

key_decisions.decision: Budget lodging at €50/night (€100 total) in a central hostel dorm, unverified
key_decisions.reasoning: No verified data, but Lisbon hostels are typically €20-60/night depending on season/location (unverified November is shoulder season, might find €40-50). Allocating €50/night as realistic minimum for central location to minimize transport costs given the short usable hours each day. This leaves €400 for everything else.
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Cheaper suburban lodging at €30/night — rejected because transport time/cost would eat into the already constrained schedule.

key_decisions.decision: Skip formal restaurants, prioritize tasca-style local spots and one pastel de nata pilgrimage
key_decisions.reasoning: Unverified: tascas (small local eateries) run €10-15/meal, whereas sit-down restaurants are €20-35. Pastéis de Belém (the famous custard tart bakery) is in Belém, likely €1-2 per tart — iconic local food hit within budget. Allocating ~€30/day for food (€90 total) by doing budget lunches and one proper dinner.
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Fine dining experience — rejected due to budget constraints (would be €50+ and consume a quarter of remaining budget).

key_decisions.decision: One nightlife evening (Bairro Alto or Alfama Fado) at ~€30-40 budget, skip the other night
key_decisions.reasoning: Unverified: Bairro Alto bar-hopping runs €3-5/drink, Fado houses charge €15-25 minimum with drink. Allocating one evening (Day 2) to nightlife to honor that interest, but can't afford both nights given budget and the need to preserve funds for transport/museums. Day 1 ends early due to travel fatigue (unverified assumption).
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Two nights out — rejected because it would add €30-40 and risk exceeding budget.
